observation.visible_scene: A nighttime fireworks display seen across a calm, dark body of water. Near the horizon sit two ground-level bursts—a smaller one on the left and a larger dome-shaped one on the right—while a broad cluster of high, sparkling blue/white bursts hangs in the sky above them. The bursts cast vertical reflections on the water. A strip of city lights with a thin vertical searchlight beam lines the left horizon, and a dark tree/land silhouette occupies the right edge. The framing of the shoreline, lights, beam, and right-side silhouette stays fixed across all frames.
visible_changes: The high blue/white sparkle clusters are brightest and most distinct in the early frames and progressively dim, thinning into faint scattered dots by the last frames.

The right ground burst evolves in place: it begins as a red radiating dome, then a bright white core ignites at its center, white radiating streaks grow over the red outline, and a purple/blue core emerges and persists through the rest of the segment.
The left ground burst likewise stays anchored in position but gains a brighter white core and develops purple/blue tints mixed with its red trails.
The water reflections mirror these changes, shifting from predominantly red/white streaks to including purple/blue reflections as the ground bursts change color.

The horizontal positions of all bursts, the city lights, the vertical beam, and the right silhouette do not move, indicating the camera is static and the changes are brightness/color/structure evolution rather than translation.
outside_clip_unknowns: The launch or onset of the high sparkle clusters (already in progress at t=0).
Whether the bursts continue, fade, or new shells appear after t=3.337.
The cause of the color transitions (shell composition) and of the dimming.
Any camera motion or framing changes outside this cropped window.
uncertain_details: Whether the high clusters drift slightly downward or only fade in place (spark positions change subtly).
Exact timing and mechanism of the purple/blue cores appearing in the ground bursts.
Precise distinction between the growing radiating streaks (expansion of the burst pattern) and simple brightening.
